chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no problem for the man to recite the Quran in the bathhouse if he intends thereby the Face of Allah, and he does not want to look at how (good) his voice is.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to recite the Quran in the bathroom or bathhouse according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), highlighting the distinction between general impurity and the permissibility of Quranic recitation in the hammam when done for Allah's sake. The hadith adds a nuanced psychological dimension by warning against *riya* (showing off) through self-admiration of one's voice, ensuring the act remains purely devotional rather than performative. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the inner state (*ikhlas*) accompanying physical acts of worship.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahimm, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no problem for the man that he should recite the Quran in the bathhouse, when he intends the Face of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> by it, and he does not want to look at how (good) his voice was’.
en.sarwar: 32. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Rib‘iy ibn ‘ Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if ’Amir al-Mu’minin prohibited reading al-Quran in a bathhouse.
He (the Imam) said, ’No, he did not prohibit. He however, prohibited reading while nude but if one has a loincloth on him, then it is not harmful.
